title: Viral Inactivation of Clinical Samples
author: Tammy Krylova
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfadjia6
materials: Discard inner bag into dry waste bag.
Pick up a new inactivation tube.
Keep pastette hovering above liquid waste container.
Return sample vial to the rack.
Discard the pastette into the liquid waste container.
Wipe over inactivation vial with Amphospray-soaked paper towel.
Stick the barcode label to the inactivation tube.
Spray the inner bag with Amphospray.
Aspirate the lysis buffer into opened swab vial.
Replace the lid on the swab container.
Replace the lid on the inactivation tube.
Pick up the corresponding swab container.
Spray box and transfer to corridor.
Notify runners that samples are ready.

steps.title: Prepare MBSC Workspace
steps.instruction: Set up the Microbiological Safety Cabinet (MBSC) for single-sample processing.

substeps.instruction: Remove the liquid waste container lid and place it to the side in the MBSC.

steps.title: Verify Sample and Barcodes
steps.instruction: Ensure sample integrity and barcode alignment before processing.

substeps.instruction: Examine the sample within the bag for leakages on the bag or tube.
Verify that the barcodes stapled to the outer bag match the barcode on the swab vial; if they do not align, do not process.
Remove barcodes and place them on the work area.

steps.title: Decontaminate and Extract Sample Vial
steps.instruction: Use Amphospray to safely remove the sample vial from its packaging.

substeps.instruction: Thoroughly soak a tissue with Amphospray.
Open the outer bag and spray the inside so the inner bag is wet.
Remove the inner bag and discard the outer bag into the dry waste bag.
Open the inner bag.
If two samples are present in one bag, take 50% of the liquid from each sample.
Remove the sample vial by either tipping it onto the wet tissue or pinching the bottom of the tube through the bag and scrunching the bag to reveal the sample.
Wipe the sample tube thoroughly with the wet tissue and place it into the rack.

steps.title: Prepare Inactivation Tube
steps.instruction: Prepare the tube that will receive the sample for inactivation.

substeps.instruction: Check that the inactivation tube contains inactivation liquid (or 1 mL L6 lysis buffer for dry swabs); discard any vial lacking liquid into the liquid waste container.
Select the best-quality barcode, ensuring labels are oriented vertically and straight for downstream automation.
Stick the barcode label to the inactivation tube and place the tube into the rack.

steps.title: Transfer Sample to Inactivation Tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the sample contents into the inactivation vial using a pastette.

substeps.instruction: Remove the swab sample from the rack and open the lid.
Place the lid into the liquid waste container (discard the swab if it is still affixed to the lid).
Hold the swab vial slightly above the liquid waste container to catch drips.
Draw up ~100 µL of swab vial contents into a fresh pastette.
Remove the lid of the inactivation vial.
Dispense the pastette's content into the bottom of the inactivation vial to minimize bubbling.
Seal the inactivation vial.
Draw up 10% Surfanios into the pastette and place it in an Eppendorf rack.
Place the open swab vial into the liquid waste container.

steps.title: Process Dry Swabs
steps.instruction: Follow specific recovery steps for dry swabs in various containers (Universal tubes or Urine pots).

substeps.instruction: Perform sample verification and extraction using Amphospray as described in previous steps.
Unscrew the barcoded 2 ml inactivation tube containing 1 mL L6 lysis buffer.
Draw up the lysis buffer into a fresh pastette and dispense it into the swab container.
Agitate the swab container to ensure swabs contact the lysis buffer.
For flat-bottomed containers, place them on an angled rack and rotate so the swab sits in the lysis buffer.
Leave tubes two spaces apart on the rack.

steps.title: Lysis Incubation and Recovery
steps.instruction: Allow dry swabs to incubate in lysis buffer before final transfer.

substeps.instruction: After adding lysis buffer to the last sample of a set (usually 12), set a 10-minute timer.
Remove over-sleeves and outer gloves, then exit the MBSC.
Outside the MBSC, put on a fresh pair of outer gloves and over-sleeves.
Wait for the 10-minute timer to sound before continuing.
Unscrew the barcoded 2 ml inactivation tube and place the lid to the side.
Verify that the barcodes on the swab container and the inactivation tube match.
Unscrew the swab container lid and discard it into the 10% Surfanios liquid waste tub.
Draw up the lysis buffer from the swab container into a fresh pastette (note: full 1 mL recovery is not expected as dry swabs absorb liquid).
Dispose of the swab container into the 10% Surfanios liquid waste tub.
Dispense the pastette's content into the bottom of the 2 ml inactivation tube to minimize bubbling.
Draw up 10% Surfanios into the pastette and replace the lid on the inactivation tube.

steps.title: Decontaminate and Remove Racks
steps.instruction: Decontaminate the rack and transfer the inactivated samples.

substeps.instruction: Visually inspect all inactivation vials to ensure they are capped.
Place the lid loosely on the liquid waste container and dispose of bags, barcodes, and blue roll into the blue waste bag.
Create a clean area in the MBSC by spraying Amphospray onto a tissue and wiping, or spraying the floor directly.
Spray the rack thoroughly with Amphospray and place it on the pre-cleaned area.
Remove 'dirty' second gloves and over-sleeves and discard them.
Wait for the timer to ring, then remove the rack from the MBSC using clean orange or blue gloves.
Transfer completed inactivation vials to the transport rack.

steps.title: Batch and Package for Transport
steps.instruction: Organize inactivated samples into racks and transfer boxes for automation.

substeps.instruction: Fill each blue lid rack with 93 inactivated samples, leaving the final three spaces for one positive and two negative controls.
Place the rack in the transfer box and replace the lid.
Close the box and apply a removable tape label with the date, time, and room.
Once the box is full, place an 'outgoing' laminated sign on the box, spray and wipe the box, and move it to the corridor table.
Phone the sample reception area to inform SHS that the box is ready for collection.

steps.title: Runner Transport to RNA Lab
steps.instruction: Transport the transfer box from CL2/3 to the RNA extraction lab.

substeps.instruction: Put on gloves in the gowning room.
Spray the outside of the transfer box with Amphospray and wipe down with a tissue.
Discard the tissue in the room waste bin.
Place the transfer box on the table by the exit.
Remove and hang up lab coat, then remove gloves and dispose of them in the blue autoclave bin.
Take the transfer box into the gowning room, wash hands, and deposit samples at the RNA extraction lab reception area.
